titleEn: Agtrinsic Expands AI Disease Intelligence Technology to South Asia’s Smallholder Farmers
titleZh: Agtrinsic将AI病害智能技术扩展至南亚小农户
summaryZh: Agtrinsic宣布在南亚推出其病害智能引擎，初期聚焦让小农户获得先进作物病害技术。公司将与当地团队合作开发反映本地作物、病害威胁、耕作方式和语言需求的移动应用，提供病害风险预警、田间指导和实用建议。该技术不同于依赖静态环境阈值或历史模式的传统预测系统，能提供持续更新的病害情报。公司还探索与农资零售商、加工商、合作社等合作，并认为本地合作模式对技术落地至关重要。
featuredReason: 该新闻展示了AI病害智能技术在新兴市场小农户中的落地模式，其本地化合作开发和移动端交付策略对智慧农业企业拓展市场具有参考价值。
contentFull:
By AgPR 

 

 Share

 

 

 

 

 

 Agtrinsic has announced the introduction of its Disease Intelligence Engine in South Asia, with an initial focus on making advanced crop disease technology accessible to smallholder farmers.

 Agtrinsic is working with a team based in the region to develop and bring a mobile application to market that reflects local crops, disease threats, farming practices and language needs. The initiative is intended to place practical disease intelligence directly into the hands of farmers who often have limited access to advanced agronomic tools and early-warning systems.

 Smallholder farmers are a vital part of regional agriculture and global food security. They produce food for their families, communities and broader supply chains while often facing crop disease with fewer technical, financial and advisory resources than larger farming operations.

 “Some of the farmers who can benefit most from earlier disease information have historically had the least access to it,” said Scott Plato, Director, Agronomy Innovation and Technology. “Our goal is to change that by making this technology practical, affordable and accessible to the smallholder farmer.”

 The South Asia initiative will build on Agtrinsic’s Disease Intelligence Engine, an artificial intelligence platform designed to provide a continuously updated view of crop disease risk as conditions change. The technology is intended to help farmers recognize developing threats earlier, prioritize scouting and make more informed crop protection decisions.

 The platform represents a different approach from traditional disease forecasting systems that rely heavily on static environmental thresholds, historical patterns, or visible symptoms. Agtrinsic’s technology is designed to provide evolving disease intelligence that can be delivered through a mobile experience suited to local production conditions.

 “We are not simply taking a product developed for large-scale agriculture and introducing it into a new market,” Plato said. “We are working with people in the region to organically build an experience around the needs of local farmers, crops and agricultural communities.”

 Agtrinsic expects the mobile application to support locally important crops and diseases while providing alerts, field-level guidance and practical recommendations through an accessible digital platform. The company is also exploring collaboration with agricultural retailers, processors, exporters, cooperatives, spray service providers and other organizations that support smallholder farming communities.

 The regional team will assist with product development, localization, field testing, farmer engagement and commercial introduction. Agtrinsic believes this local partnership model will be critical to ensuring the technology is relevant, trusted and usable in everyday farming decisions.

 “Protecting the productivity of farms is not just a local agricultural issue,” said Matt Free, Vice President of Agronomy. “It is directly connected to food availability, rural livelihoods and the resilience of the global food system. When these farmers have better tools to protect their crops, the benefits extend far beyond a region.”

 The South Asia launch is part of Agtrinsic’s broader effort to make advanced disease intelligence available across diverse crops, farming systems and geographies. The technology is the subject of pending U.S. and international patent applications.

 Additional details about the application, regional availability and field programs will be announced as development and testing progress.

translationZh:
Agtrinsic已宣布在南亚推出其病害智能引擎，初期重点是让先进作物病害技术惠及小农户。

Agtrinsic正与该地区的一个团队合作，开发和推出一款移动应用，以反映当地作物、病害威胁、耕作方式和语言需求。该计划旨在将实用的病害智能直接交到农民手中，而这些农民往往难以获得先进农艺工具和早期预警系统。

小农户是区域农业和全球粮食安全的重要组成部分。他们为家庭、社区和更广泛的供应链生产粮食，同时往往比大型农场面临更少的技术、资金和咨询服务来应对作物病害。

“一些最能从更早的病害信息中受益的农民，历史上却最少获得这些信息，”农艺创新与技术总监Scott Plato表示。“我们的目标是通过让这项技术对小农户实用、可负担且易于获取来改变这一现状。”

南亚计划将建立在Agtrinsic的病害智能引擎之上，这是一个AI平台，旨在随着条件变化提供持续更新的作物病害风险视图。该技术旨在帮助农民更早识别正在发展的威胁，优先安排田间巡查，并做出更明智的作物保护决策。

该平台代表了一种不同于传统病害预报系统的方法，后者严重依赖静态环境阈值、历史模式或可见症状。Agtrinsic的技术旨在提供不断演变的病害智能，并可通过适合当地生产条件的移动体验来传递。

“我们不是简单地把为大规模农业开发的产品引入新市场，”Plato说。“我们正在与该地区的人们合作，围绕当地农民、作物和农业社区的需求有机地构建一种体验。”

Agtrinsic预计该移动应用将支持当地重要作物和病害，同时通过易于访问的数字平台提供警报、田间指导和实用建议。该公司还在探索与农资零售商、加工商、出口商、合作社、喷雾服务提供商以及其他支持小农户社区的组织合作。

区域团队将协助产品开发、本地化、田间测试、农民参与和商业引入。Agtrinsic认为，这种本地合作模式对于确保技术在日常农业决策中具有相关性、可信度和可用性至关重要。

“保护农场生产力不仅仅是一个地方农业问题，”农艺副总裁Matt Free表示。“它直接关系到粮食供应、农村生计和全球粮食系统的韧性。当这些农民拥有更好的工具来保护作物时，益处将远远超出该地区。”

南亚发布是Agtrinsic更广泛努力的一部分，旨在让先进病害智能适用于不同作物、农业系统和地理区域。该技术正在申请美国和国际贸易专利。

有关该应用、区域可用性和田间计划的更多细节将在开发和测试进展中公布。
